groups.name: Cash
items: Get yen from 7-Eleven (Seven Bank) ATMs with a debit card. Skip exchanging before the trip.
When the ATM offers a currency, choose yen, never USD.
Check your bank's foreign ATM fees before you go, and carry a backup card or about $100 in case a card gets declined.

groups.name: Getting around
items: One physical Suica or Welcome Suica each covers trains, subways, buses, konbini and vending machines nationwide.
Riding an express takes the base fare (Suica at the gate) plus a seat ticket. smartEX and the N’EX round trip bundle both; Romancecar seats on EMot don’t.
If a foreign card fails online, any JR ticket office sells the same tickets.

groups.name: Tax-free
items: Since Nov 1, 2026: pay full price, passport scanned at purchase, claim the 10% at the airport before security.

groups.name: Luggage
items: Takkyubin from any hotel front desk; Yamato counters are in most hotels.
Bags over 160 cm total on the Shinkansen need a seat with an oversized baggage area, free to reserve, ¥1,000 fee without one.
Never abandon an old suitcase. Ask the store that sells you the new one, then the hotel front desk (about ¥2,000), then the airport luggage shop.

groups.name: Shopping
items: Sony and Sigma lenses bought in Japan usually carry a Japan-only warranty. Compare on kakaku.com first.
